Scenarios, Sector Implications, s-t uncertainty, l-t fundas
strong

PO:350.00 USD   |   Price:186.64 USD  
| Equity   |   09 November 2026  
---

---  
Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * NVDA review of foreign-intelligence concerns adds governance/policy overhang, but allegations are not proven business damage
  * Scenarios: 1) Containment and a refocus on fundas, 2) prolonged uncertainty on valuation, 3) escalation/tighter restrictions
  * Valuation provides support: SOX already down 37% at 13.7x fwd PE (22% below SPX), only 12% from 12x historical trough

  
---  
| FULL REPORT|     |   
---|---|---  
  
* * *  
  
---  
  
New overhang, not yet an earnings event

NVIDIA's independent review of reported foreign-intelligence concerns adds
governance and policy uncertainty; the board says it has no reason to believe
company secrets or national security were compromised. The investment debate
is whether this remains company-specific or triggers restrictions and
disruption across AI infrastructure. We would not equate allegations with
proven business damage.

Three scenarios, three investment outcomes

We see: 1) containment, with leadership continuity and no material findings
allowing fundamentals to regain focus; 2) prolonged uncertainty, pressuring
valuation before earnings; 3) escalation, with adverse findings, leadership
disruption or tighter restrictions requiring earnings reassessment. Conviction
rests on distinguishing headline risk from changes in customer access, orders
and execution, not assuming a quick resolution.

Ecosystem funding is a second transmission risk

A more cautious approach to new ecosystem investments could slow funding-
dependent AI projects, affecting memory, networking and equipment demand
beyond NVIDIA. This is a scenario, not an announced response. Alternative
capital could fill the gap; less visible dealmaking need not mean less
support. The key question is whether spending shifts between suppliers or is
delayed across the ecosystem.

China exposure could outweigh share gains

In case of potential distractions or increased scrutiny at NVDA, other compute
suppliers such as AMD, Broadcom and Marvell could gain additional traction.
However if NVDA distractions also increased scrutiny, then any US supplier
selling to China including compute, networking, semicap, EDA could face more
volatility. Trailing edge suppliers in analog, microcontrollers could be less
exposed, in our view. .

Storm before the calm; valuation matters

Friday's SOX snapshot
showed a 37% correction, 13.7x forward PE and a 22% discount to SPX. A
historical ~12x trough implied ~12% further downside on unchanged estimates,
not a floor. Our cycle work suggested a trough could be within one quarter.
Earnings cuts remain a risk, but policy clarity, quantified resets and
buybacks could restore confidence. We remain constructive on recovery as
uncertainty becomes measurable.

| | The concern for memory is less about delayed data center builds (post US elections) or AI demand, than the risk of a '2028 earnings cliff' narrative, where the market remains skeptical about growth momentum for memory as supply begins to catch-up with demand. New Top Pick is Samsung Electronics.   
---  
  
A little too far, too fast... The memory AI trade derating has been going on
for months - as discussed in _Tech Bytes: Memory – Changing Tides (6 Jul
2026)_
– and culminated in heavy selling last week amid investor concerns that the US
mid-term election outcome could delay data center builds – if we have fewer
data centers to put chips in, will capex fall? This raised further concerns
around earnings achievability and sustainability beyond 2027.

… but can we avoid the '2028 earnings cliff' narrative? Near-term memory
fundamentals look to be intact (demand, capital returns), but that is not
investors' key concern – the debate has moved to the 2028 supply response, as
new capacity entering production raises the prospect of a meaningful change in
supply-demand conditions. In this demand-led super cycle, exceptional returns
bring on new supply, but this will have eventual consequences for those
returns and ultimately for share prices.

Share prices lead fundamentals, discounting the risk that earnings may need to
come down in the next couple of years as supply catches up and the AI build
out slows. We reduce our through-cycle long-term margin assumptions towards
historical averages, which lowers our multiples and price targets offsetting
lower share counts from buybacks. Our Hynix price target falls 38% to W1.6m
and our Samsung price targets fall 19% to W309k for the ordinary shares and
W247,200 for the prefs.

Late-cycle investing. As highlighted in _Tech Bytes: Memory – Cycles vs.
Super Cycles (11 Oct
2026)_
, AI makes memory structural but it is still cyclical with 7x the amplitude,
with the market continuing to reward those who priced it first. Investor
sentiment has become much more bearish, and valuations already reflect
considerable concern about earnings durability, but we are late cycle, so
returns are harder to come by and generally favor the largest, best
capitalized, scaled tech leaders. Hence, Samsung Electronics becomes our new
Top Pick. Read

| | | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * VST '26 and '27 guidance raise, Cogentrix close, and contracting opportunities remain in tact 
  * CEG '26 guidance raised, Peak+ could offer more contracting upside 
  * NRG 3Q EBITDA beat and largely in-line guidance for '27; Announced $4b assets sale to fund incremental buybacks and growth opportunities

VST (OW): 3Q beat and '26 and '27 guidance raises, although largely in line w/
cons.; contracting opportunity set remains despite election results.

  * Financial results: 3Q beat, 2026 guidance narrowed, and formal 2027 guidance initiated. Adj. EBITDA was $2,378m in 3Q26, +11% above cons. of $2,140m (MS: $2,125m). Management narrowed 2026 EBITDA guidance to $7.1B-$7.5B (from $6.8B-$7.6B), midpoint in line w/ cons. of $7.3B (MS: $7.2B). The company also initiated formal 2027 Adj. EBITDA guidance at $7.7B-$8.5B (from an initial midpoint opportunity of $7.4B-$7.8B excluding Cogentrix and Meta), midpoint +1% above cons. of $8.0B (MS: $7.4B). We would note that the company's $7.7B-$8.5B range reflects the recent Cogentrix close and the first phase of the Meta operating PPA, while MSe does not include those items. '26 FCFbG guidance was narrowed to $4,300m-$4,700m (from $3,925m-$4,725m) (MS: $4,181m) and '27 FCFbG guidance was initiated at $4,300m-$5,100m (MS: $4,232).
  * Cogentrix adds scale and expected cash flow accretion. Vistra closed its Cogentrix acquisition in October, increasing the fleet by ~5,500MW and further diversifying assets across ERCOT, PJM, and ISO-NE. The deal’s expected adj. free cash flow accretion has improved since it was announced, to high-single digits in the near term and double digits beginning in 2029. 
  * Texas election outcome does not change Vistra’s view of the opportunity. Following the midterm election results on Tuesday, management remained confident in its fundamental outlook for the state. Clearer direction from policymakers could help move customer projects forward by reducing uncertainty, and the team noted that many of the concerns around data centers have been widespread across the country and in the markets prior to the elections. 
  * Contracting opportunities span existing nuclear and gas assets, as well as new build. Management described customer engagement as robust across the portfolio and said it remains confident in pursuing additional nuclear PPAs. Beaver Valley and the second portion of Comanche Peak remain uncontracted, with additional uprate potential at Comanche Peak. We embed ~$21/share into our base PT considering contracts at the remaining ~3GW of open nuclear capacity. Management also mentioned ongoing discussions around existing gas plants and new gas build, with the 20-year, 207MW Odessa agreement with New Era as an example of recent progress.
  * Share repurchases: VST reiterated its capital-allocation plan of at least $1B of share repurchases and $300m of dividends annually. The company now has $2.5B remaining on current buyback authorizations through 2028 (prior $1.2B through 2027). 
  * Power prices and hedges: The company has hedged 98% and 78% of expected generation volumes for '27 and '28, respectively (vs. 94% and 72% as of 2Q26). Importantly, the company reiterated confidence in the LT fundamentals, with annual load growth of at least 4-6% in ERCOT and 2-3% in PJM through 2030.

CEG (OW): 3Q EPS beat and '26 guidance raise

  * Financial results: Adj. EPS of $5.06, +31% above cons. of $3.86 (MS: $3.89). CEG raised its ’26 EPS guidance for the second time this year to $12.50-$12.80 (from $11.50-$12.50), +5% above cons. of $12.04 (MS: $12.14). Reiterated base earnings guidance in '26, '27 and '29. Reaffirmed target base EPS growth of 20%+ from '26-'29 and LT rolling 3yr base EPS growth of 10%+.
  * 1,165 MW uprates to cost $4.3bn, including $3b of incremental growth capex during '28–'32.
  * Peak+ adds another lever to contracting pathway. First agreement benefits from 20-year term with an IG data economy customer. 270 MW from the existing nuclear paired with new generation and demand response.
  * Grid clarity to come during 1H27. PJM/RTO compliance filings due in the coming weeks, followed by FERC action in 2027, potentially in 1Q.

  * Share repurchases: CEG has deployed $3b in buyback YTD, leaving $2b remaining in the $5b of authorized share-repurchase plan. The company expects to complete the program by end of 2027 and plans to update the buyback plan on or before the 4Q call. 
  * 4Q guidance will update both base and enhanced earnings assumptions for 2027 and 2028. The current guidance is for enhanced earnings of 30-40% of total earnings. 2026 commercial gains and generation outperformance may not recur. As generation move into contracts, more earnings enter the base category and the enhanced contribution could decline.

NRG (EW): 3Q EBITDA beat and largely in-line guidance for '27; Announced $4b
assets sale to fund incremental buybacks and growth opportunities.

  * Financial results: Adj. EBITDA of $2,013m in 3Q, +12% above cons. of $1,799m (MS: $1,851m). Reiterated 

2026 Adj. EBITDA of $5,325-$5,825m, midpoint +1% above cons. of $5,500m (MS:
$5,421m) – with the good performance in 3Q NRG expects to be slightly below
the mid-point despite the unfavorable pricing environment in Texas in 2026.
The company initiated 2027 Adj. EBITDA guidance at $5,500-$6,000m, midpoint
-1% below cons. of $5,837m (MS: $5,758m). Guidance includes the assets that
are being sold, and NRG will update numbers after the transaction closes
(expected in the 2Q26).

  * Assets sale announcement: NRG announced the sale of six gas plants to LS Power for $4b (implying 8x EV/EBITDA '27), totaling 4.9 GW across NYISO (Ravenswood), ISO-NE (Ocean State Power and Wallingford), and ERCOT (Jack County, Johnson County, and R.W. Miller). Proceeds will be used to increase buybacks by $1b, reduce debt by $2b and leave $1b with flexibility to fund either contracted growth investments or additional debt reduction. Valuation looks attractive from an EV/EBITDA perspective, consistent with our fair value assumption for gas assets and well above the multiple implied in the current stock price, although we note that 2027 EBITDA is likely a low year. Strategically, we like the divestment of non-core regions (NY and NE) and at the current stock price the monetization coupled with increased buybacks look accretive. 
  * Data center BYOP deal: NRG reiterated its target to announce the 1.2 GW Bring Your Own Power (BYOP) data center deal by the end of the year – the parties made meaningful progress since the 2Q update. Management sees the pipeline of BYOP projects exceeding NRG's framework agreements with GEV and Kiewit and ruled out monetizing its turbine reservations. The primary funding source for the project will likely be a financial partner, which would ideally be announced by the end of the year but could slip into early 2027. 
  * Texas power prices: ERCOT power prices have been impacted by the meaningful new builds of battery and solar projects in the last 2 years, and demand growth was not enough to surpass that supply increase. Management sees strong load growth tailwinds in Texas going forward, driven not only by data centers but also by multi GWs of manufacturing demand growth, which should take some of the excess capacity. NRG locked low power prices for 2027 to protect short-term cash flows, but remains highly confident on long-term prices.

More or Less in-line

---  
| | AlphaSignals Earnings Reaction   
---  
| | | **Unchanged**  
---|---  
|  Impact to our thesis  
| | **In-line**  
---|---  
|  Financial results versus consensus  
| | **Largely
unchanged**  
---|---  
|  Direction of next 12-month consensus EPS  
Source: Company data, Morgan Stanley Research  
| | Key takeaways  
---  
  
  * Offers in-line FY27 guide (c.€20bn) on increase in AI D/C demand ("close" to €4bn) and guides GM%/Seg% to mid-to-high 40s% and mid-20s% respectively. 
  * Q4 gave in-line sales (€4.71bn) , slightly better segment result (€1.12bn vs €1.10bn) but a marginally weaker EPS (60c vs 64c). 
  * Q1 sales/margins in-line with expectations with €4.6bn sales and c.23% segment - Autos and PS stable, whilst ES declines moderately 
  * FY27 helped by strength in PS, autos up mid-teens% and edge up low teens% - €3.0-3.5bn capex guide (mainly Dresden, SiC/Kulim, Villach 300mm). 
  * The analyst call is at 09:30 CET today. 

  
  
First Take. The growth in PS, driven by data centres, next year continues to
do well. Our view was a number closer to €3.6bn (FY26 : €2.2bn, including
classic DC) with close to c.€4bn for AI DC (incl. classic). Automotive
meantime seems to be improving better next year than we had assumed (mid-
teens% growth vs HSD-LDD% Ms/e), we think due to MCU traction in SDVs. We
expect edge to be in recovery and industrials to benefit from continued AI
infrastructure trends. Margins, described again as mid-to-high 40s%, straddle
consensus (c.47%) for FY27, the segment result (guided to mid-20s%) is also
in-line. Infineon ups the guide for investments at €3.0-3.5bn, with focus on
build-out of capacity for the AI data centre ramp (mainly at Dresden). The Q1
sales guide is in-line with expectations at c.€4.6bn sales (cons €4.6bn) with
most segments flat qq.

Infineon: Comparing Actuals with Consensus
 Source: Company data,
